title: Georgia Tech’s Nexus AI supercomputer can now be accessed by all US scientists
key_facts: Georgia Tech has opened nationwide access to Nexus, its new AI supercomputer at the Coda Data Center in Atlanta.
Nexus was built with a $20 million investment from the National Science Foundation (NSF) in partnership with the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
It combines simulation, large datasets and AI model building on one platform.
90 percent of its computing capacity is allocated through an open, peer-reviewed process coordinated by NSF.
Targeted fields include drug discovery, energy, neuroscience and robotics.
Ángel Cabrera, president of Georgia Tech, and Irina Dolinskaya of NSF commented in a press release.
quote_evidence: As a national resource, 90 percent of the computing capacity will be available through an open, peer-reviewed allocation process that will be coordinated by the NSF.
why_it_matters_hint: US researchers outside big labs can apply for time on a national AI-and-simulation machine.
notes: Date of the access opening is not given in the article.
